# Set up SAML SSO

This topic describes how to set up SAML SSO for HCP, as well as how to update your SSO integration for compatibility with changes to HCP SAML support. 

## Requirements

Verify that you meet the following requirements.

### Permissions 

@include 'requirements/sso.mdx'

### Supported identity providers

HCP supports SAML SSO with the following identity providers (IdP):

- Auth0
- AWS
- Azure Entra ID
- Cyberark
- Duo Security
- Google Cloud
- IBM Verify
- JumpCloud
- Okta
- One Login
- PingID


@include 'hcp-administration/verify-domain.mdx'

## Enable a new SAML SSO for HCP

<Warning>

If you use SAML SSO, you must update the SSO Sign-On URL in your identity provider before January 31, 2027, or users will be unable to sign in. Refer to [Migrate an existing SAML SSO configuration](#migrate-an-existing-saml-sso-configuration) for instructions. OIDC SSO is not affected.

</Warning>

You must configure SSO settings in HCP, as well as configure your identity provider.

### Initiate integration on HCP

1. [Log in to HCP](https://portal.cloud.hashicorp.com/) and go to your organization.
1. From your organization, click **Organization settings**.
1. Click **SSO**, and then click **Configure SSO for your organization**.
1. Select **SAML**.
1. Copy the following values to enter into your identity provider.

   - **SSO Sign-On URL**
   - **Entity ID**
   - **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

Open a new tab in your web browser to continue the configuration with your preferred identity provider.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="Auth0">

### Configure Auth0

Follow the steps to [manually configure Auth0 SSO integrations](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/single-sign-on/outbound-single-sign-on/configure-auth0-saml-identity-provider#manually-configure-sso-integrations).

Enter the following values from HCP into your Auth0 environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="AWS">

### Configure AWS

Follow the steps to [set up single sign-on access to your applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/set-up-single-sign-on-access-to-applications.html).

Enter the following values from HCP into your AWS environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Azure">

### Configure Azure

Follow the steps to [integrate a private application in the Azure documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/add-application-portal-setup-sso).

Enter the following values from HCP into your Azure environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="CyberArk">

Enter the following values from HCP into your CyberArk environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**

- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Duo Security">

### Configure Duo Security

Follow the steps for [Duo Single Sign-On for Generic SAML Service Providers](https://duo.com/docs/sso-generic)

Enter the following values from HCP into your Duo Security environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Google">

### Configure Google

Enter the following values from HCP into your Google Cloud environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="JumpCloud">

### Configure JumpCloud

Follow the steps to [Get Started: SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) in the JumpCloud documentation](https://jumpcloud.com/support/get-started-applications-saml-sso#using-sso-applications-with-jumpcloud).

Enter the following values from HCP into your JumpCloud environment.

- **SSO Sign-On URL**
- **Entity ID**
- **Email Attribute Assertion Name**

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Okta">

### Configure Okta

Follow the steps to [integrate a private application in the Okta documentation](https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/add-private-app/saml2/main/).

Enter the following values from HCP into your Okta environment. If your Okta organization uses Okta Identity Engine (OIE), configure the **Email Attribute Assertion Name** under the **Sign On** tab after completing the Okta creation wizard.

<Tab heading="One Login">

Follow the steps to set up the [Advanced SAML Custom Connector](https://onelogin.service-now.com/support?id=kb_article&sys_id=8a1f3d501b392510c12a41d5ec4bcbcc).

<Tab heading="PingID">

Follow the steps to [add a SAML application](https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingone/pingone_tutorials/p1_p1tutorial_add_a_saml_app.html).

### Continue integration on HCP

Return to HCP. Enter the following information from your identity provider.

- **SAML IDP Single Sign-On URL**
- **SAML IDP Certificate**

## Complete SSO setup

1. Assign a [default organization role](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso/default-role) for users.
1. Optionally, turn on **Assign users an organization role**.
1. Click **Save**.

If you complete the integration before January 31, 2027, you must [migrate your existing SAML SSO configuration](#migrate-an-existing-saml-sso-configuration) so that users can sign in.

## Migrate an existing SAML SSO configuration

You may only need to complete this action if you configured SAML SSO before January 31, 2027. If so, HCP prints an **Action required** banner at the top of the page. If you do not see this banner, then your organization is already up to date and no additional action is necessary.

1. [Log in to HCP](https://portal.cloud.hashicorp.com/) and go to your organization.
1. Click **Update SSO settings** in the banner to proceed to the SAML configuration page.
1. The SAML configuration page opens in read-only mode. Click **Start migration** to proceed.
1. Copy the URL in the **Copy the new URL** field.
1. If your IdP requires a signing certificate, open the **View signing certificate** menu, then click **Download certificate**.
1. In your IdP settings, paste the URL you copied in step 4 into the appropriate field. Refer to [Initiate integration on HCP](#initiate-integration-on-hcp) for information about supported IdP settings.
1. Select **I have updated my IdP** to confirm that you have updated the SSO Sign-On URL in your identity provider.
1. Click **Apply update and continue** to complete the update.
1. When prompted, complete the steps to test your connection and verify that the migration was successful. 
1. If the migration was successful, click **Close migration wizard** to exit. Otherwise, complete the [steps to roll back the migration](#roll-back-the-migration).

### Roll back the migration

If your migration was unsuccessful, complete the following steps in the migration wizard so that users can login while you investigate potential issues:

1. Select **Restore access using the previous sign-on URL**, then click **Close migration wizard**.
1. Copy the previously stored sign-in URL and download the previous signing certificate.
1. Provide your IdP with the previous URL and certificate.
1. Click **Revert migration**.
